reason: Harvesting lettuce is the only available combination and should advance the goal of eating from the garden.
expectation: I expect to cut some lettuce leaves, though preparing them to eat may require another step.

effect: The harvest produced smaller leaves despite the storm, and they are ready to take to the galley.
reaction: It is satisfying to see the sheltered bed still producing, even if the leaves are smaller.
reason: Using the leaves at the galley seems like the natural next step toward eating the harvest.
expectation: I expect to prepare or eat the storm lettuce, though it may need another step.

alternatives.reason: I considered cutting more leaves, but I already have some for the meal.

effect: The lettuce became a meal, completing the goal and showing that the protected garden can still provide fresh food during the storm.
reaction: The sound of the pump and the recorded crunch made the small harvest feel meaningful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Eating the storm-grown lettuce was most worthwhile: the meal connected the garden’s survival to a tangible reward.

leastWorthwhile.text: The harvest itself was straightforward, with only one initial choice, though it set up the meal.

surprise.text: The bed had kept growing in the darkened cabin, even though its outer leaves were smaller.

arbitrary.text: Neither action felt arbitrary; cutting the leaves and taking them to the galley both had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue to learn what happens after the storm and how the specimens reach Earth, though this short chapter offered little decision-making.
